A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaST0 research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V3 reports original RLBench experiments, real-world robotic manipulation results, inference measurements and ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds LIBERO experiments, architectural and sampling ablations, latent-space analyses and synthetic-point-cloud robustness results.

M1.justification: The MoT architecture, autoregressive latent generation, cosine and flow-matching objectives, and KV-cache procedure remain unchanged. LIBERO uses benchmark-specific modality and temporal-sampling configurations; v3 already evaluates image-plus-state latents and permits adjustable temporal granularity.

E1.justification: V4 adds LIBERO-Spatial, Object, Goal and Long, each containing ten tasks, substantially extending simulated manipulation coverage. The pretraining corpus, ten RLBench tasks and existing real-world tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: OpenVLA-OFT becomes an evaluated comparator in the new LIBERO comparison, Table 2. The six RLBench comparators and existing real-world baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added LIBERO evaluation introduces separate training per suite, two RGB views, 500 evaluation trials per suite, omitted geometric latents and latent stride 8. New analyses introduce PCA-distance measurements, a single-backbone control and substitution of synthetic 3D supervision. Retained RLBench and real-world protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Figure 5 ablations, v4 tests MoT versus a single backbone, all modality orderings and latent temporal strides. Appendices F and G add latent/action separability analyses and robustness to VGGT-generated supervision, substantially expanding tests of architectural and representational assumptions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random-seed evaluations with means and variances for RLBench and three repeated real-world evaluations. The additions introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure, significance test or disclosed repeated-run count; LIBERO results are presented as point estimates.

E6.justification: V4 adds LIBERO results, including LaST0 at 98.1% versus OpenVLA-OFT at 97.1%, plus ablation, PCA and robustness outcomes. Existing RLBench, Figure 5 and real-world scores are unchanged. New Table 2 contains inconsistent means: SpatialVLA's listed suites average 79.55%, not 78.1%, and CoT-VLA's average 83.925%, not 81.1%.

T1.justification: The latent-sequence definition, cosine loss, action-space formulations and policy factorization are retained, including the relocated method appendix. The new PCA analyses introduce empirical measurements, without new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about compact physical reasoning, dual-system coordination and efficient manipulation. The introduction adds LIBERO performance evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges limited mobile/dexterous pretraining coverage and difficulties with complex object interactions. Appendices E-G add interpretations of modality ordering, temporal spacing, latent separability and synthetic-depth robustness. The central interpretation and existing failure explanations remain intact.

D1.justification: New Appendix A/Table 4 substantially expands reproducibility information, specifying learning rates, scheduling, batch size, precision, gradient clipping, attention implementation and flow-matching settings. These are disclosures, not evidence that retained experiments changed. V4 removes the general statement about official baseline checkpoints and recommended fine-tuning configurations.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including LIBERO, OpenVLA-OFT, FreqPolicy and diffusion trajectory-guided policy, while removing works including GraspVLA, DexVLA, TinyVLA and Hao et al.'s continuous-latent reasoning paper. The overall positioning against explicit CoT remains stable; duplicate-reference cleanup does not establish further substantive changes.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 is revised around two simulation benchmarks, and limitations, acknowledgements and new appendix sections are added. Author affiliations and headings are updated, and visualization subsections are reordered. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds seven tables and a synthetic-point-cloud figure, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Figure 5 is restyled with unchanged values, Figure 6 includes additional previously illustrated tasks, and several appendix figures are relocated or renumbered. Front-page affiliation and publication formatting also changes.

improvement.justification: Table 4 improves reproducibility, while the single-backbone and synthetic-supervision controls address previously untested design assumptions; explicit limitations also improve qualification. These gains outweigh bounded reporting problems. However, the new LIBERO table understates two baseline means, and PCA distances alone do not establish the claimed modality orthogonality or causal improvements in action stability, limiting the overall quality gain.
